title: Regional water supply shortage and local response
subtitle: Cold water ice making expansion, pothole repairs, heritage designations, annual zoning update, Pitch Kitchener and police dispatch agreement.
overview: Council received a mayoral update on the Region of Waterloo's water capacity constraint in the Mannheim service area. Kitchener has activated its Incident Management Plan, and the update will become a regular item. Councillors raised development approvals, conservation, private pools, splash pads, rain barrels and support for water-intensive businesses. These were discussed without a motion.

Council approved several items that affect residents directly. These include a cold water ice making issue paper for the 2027 budget, continuing Pitch Kitchener as an annual program, the Annual Zoning By-law Update, and heritage designations for two properties. Council also supported a shared dispatch agreement for municipal by-law enforcement and approved 2026 neighbourhood association affiliations.

In question period, councillors pressed staff on this winter's potholes. Staff described overnight crews, a push on public communication and a coming review of winter service levels. Staff also said the draft Kitchener 2051 Official Plan is out for consultation and no decisions have been made on it.

decisions.detail: Staff will prepare an issue paper for the 2027 budget on expanding cold water ice making to Grand River Arena, Don McLaren Arena and the Memorial Auditorium ice pads {{vote:m9}}.
Council endorsed Pitch Kitchener as an annual initiative, subject to funding, and directed staff to bring a funding request in the 2027 budget process {{vote:m10}}.
Council approved the amendments to Zoning By-laws 85-1 and 2019-051, including a revised interior side yard setback provision, without further public notice {{vote:m8}}.
Council recognized the cultural heritage value of 20 Linden Avenue and 305 King Street West and will pursue designation under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m3}}.

Council supported a shared dispatch agreement with Waterloo Regional Police Services and other municipalities, provided Waterloo and Cambridge take part, and asked staff to request collaboration with police on city service matters {{vote:m6}}.
Council approved the 2026 list of neighbourhood associations for affiliation and added them to the City's third-party liability insurance program {{vote:m5}}.
Council approved demolition of a detached garage and construction of a new one, conditional on heritage staff clearing final building permit drawings {{vote:m2}}.

debate: On water supply, councillors asked for more information and for regional staff to appear before Council. The mayor said an all-council meeting or a caucus briefing with regional officials could be explored.
One councillor urged transparency, including public water-level data. The mayor agreed on the goal but said staff also need time to work through options, and that the balance has not yet been struck.

Councillors discussed conservation. Ideas included reviewing new private pool permits, reinstating the rain barrel program, supporting water-intensive businesses and revisiting splash pad rules. Another councillor cautioned against implying pools would be banned. Staff said municipal water uses are under review and will report back.

On the ice making motion, a councillor asked why costs would rise with expansion. Staff said equipment prices have gone up. They gave a payback of about 10 to 12 years, compared with a shorter estimate during the pilot.

On potholes, staff said cold patch often fails in wet, cold conditions and permanent repairs must wait for asphalt plants to open. Councillors asked about contracted help, using by-law vehicles to spot damage, and clearer communication.
